Hi Kim / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. We're starting to pull numbers for an initial reserved commitment and want to get guidance on which GPU mix makes sense for our workload. Quick context: our production inference is a mix of 2.5k short-chat qps (avg len 60 tokens) and 120 batch-heavy rerank jobs (avg 1.6k tokens) at peak. Memory matters for the rerank model (2.7B encoder) but the chat path is more flops/throughput bound.

Two asks:
- Can you sketch perf/$ tradeoffs for A100 (40 GB), H100 (80 GB), and L40S (48 GB) in this hybrid profile?
- What commit shapes and throughput SLAs you typically recommend that give predictable unit cost without overcommitting capacity?

I've attached a preliminary sizing table (quantedge_sizing_table.xlsx) with traffic patterns — happy to hop on a call if it's easier.

Hi Liam — thanks for the table, looks useful. Quick read-through below and a couple of high-level recommendations before we dig into numbers.

Short answers up front:
- If memory pressure from the rerank encoder is the primary constraint (model pins > 40 GB per instance), H100 80 GB avoids sharding complexity and often reduces operational risk; it comes at a higher perf/$ baseline but can lower engineering overhead and KV-cache inefficiency.
- L40S is the best perf/$ for throughput-bound short-chat when memory fits in 48 GB and you can rely on batching.
- A100 40 GB is competitive in price but becomes risky if you must shard the rerank model --- sharding increases latency variance and increases pooling needs.

Commit shape guidance:
- Start with a two-tier commit: a guaranteed reserved slab sized to cover baseline 24/7 short-chat (70% of sustained qps) + a burst pool (smaller, lower-priced) for peak rerank batch bursts. This tends to give predictable unit cost while avoiding a large upfront commit for rarely used rerank spikes.
- Throughput SLAs: offer a per-route P50/P95 latency target for chat and a throughput window (jobs/hour) for rerank with credits for bursting above the baseline.

Next steps: we'll produce a perf/$ matrix for the exact traffic in your sheet and draft a commit proposal (term lengths, credits, and CAPEX-style up-front vs monthly blends). Dropping the initial sketch by EOD tomorrow.

—Kim

Adding a few operational notes and a quick matrix from our infra experiments (high level). See inline.

- Rerank (memory-bound):
  * H100 80GB: no sharding, stable latency, best tail for KV cache hits. Perf/$ = higher baseline but ops cost lower.
  * A100 40GB: requires model sharding for 2.7B encoder in many cases — increases per-request overhead and reduces effective throughput by ~12-18% in our tests. Perf/$ appears similar to L40S when you amortize sharding overhead.
  * L40S 48GB: borderline for some larger optimizer states; if you can quantize and remove optimizer artifacts, it's usually fine and cheaper.

- Short-chat (throughput-bound):
  * L40S (48GB): best perf/$ when batch sizes are > 8 and latencies are tolerant of micro-batching.
  * H100: excellent for single-request p95-sensitive workloads but expensive if you rely on sustained micro-batch throughput.

Suggested numbers for your sheet (we'll validate in the perf run):
- Baseline reserved slab: 16 x L40S (covers ~70% of sustained short-chat with batching)
- Rerank dedicated nodes: 6 x H100 (handles peak rerank with clean tails; avoids sharding operational work)
- Burst pool (shared): 8 x A100 (cheaper burst capacity for mixed workloads, used only for non-p95-sensitive jobs)

Costing model idea (to align incentives):
- Reserved slab: deeper discount (committed, monthly) with soft credits that roll into burst pool usage.
- Rerank dedicated: higher SLA/backstop with a smaller committed discount, or a usage-based premium for guaranteed tail.

I'm attaching a one-page matrix (we'll produce numbers tonight) and a draft of term options.

Summary (high level):
- Hybrid portfolio recommended: L40S-heavy reserved slab for chat (perf/$), H100 for rerank tail stability, A100 burst pool for price-efficient capacity on episodic spikes.
- Suggested initial term: 12 months with a quarterly review to right-size pool counts after two production months.
- Pricing packaging: two-tier discounting — slab (deeper discount) + dedicated tail nodes (moderate discount) + metered burst credits. We will propose a blended effective perf/$ in the draft term sheet.
